target_zone_range.evidence_basis: South-central Texas floristic voucher set explicitly records G. pumila in Uvalde, Medina, and Real counties; Travis and Williamson are also independently documented.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Exact county vouchers used; no broad ecoregion inference.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with overall scale and leaf shape. Low verbena stays compact and low, with small broadly ovate leaves divided into a few broader lobes rather than the much finer feathery dissection of prairie verbena. Its short, dense flower spike remains compact instead of stretching strongly in fruit.
diagnostic_traits: annual, low and spreading to ascending
often under 20 cm tall in Williamson material
small broadly ovate leaves with 3–6 paired lobes and sublobes
young foliage velvety with nonglandular and stalked glandular hairs
inflorescence axis does not strongly elongate in fruit

confusers.separator: G. bipinnatifida has larger, more deeply and finely 1–2-pinnately dissected leaves and generally a coarser, more feathery appearance. G. pumila is the smaller, compact, broad-lobed plant.
